title: Remission: guilt-relation ceases; reconciling relation arises by the gospel law of faith and repentance
source_text: XIII. Jam vero remissio peccatorum in eo sita est, quod in homine cesset relatio illa quae reatus vocatur, & ejus loco alia exurgat, ratione cujus homo dicitur Deo reconciliatus, & a peccato absolutus. Sicut ergo reatus, posito peccato resultat, vi aeternae legis jam dictae, & in verbo Dei publicatae: ita quoque peccato per veram poenitentiam retractato atque derelicto, & posita fide actuosa, qua peccator ad Dei clementiam in Christo confugiat, cessat relatio illa per quam peccator obnoxius erat maledictioni & irae divinae, & exurgit alia per quam Deo gratus est, & ad vitam aeternam acceptus, idque vi legis alterius, qua Deus etiam ab aeterno sanxit, ut peccator omnis per veram contritionem a peccato recedens, & misericordiam divinam serio implorans, ac per fidem vivam & efficacem amplectens, immunis esset a poenis quae peccato debentur, & Deo fieret gratus & amicus, jusque ad vitam aeternam haberet: quam legem Deus quoque in verbo suo publicari curavit.
pass_a_gloss: Now indeed the remission of sins is situated in this, that in the man that relation which is called guilt ceases, and in its place another arises by reason of which the man is said to be reconciled to God and absolved from sin. Just as therefore guilt, sin being posited, results by force of the eternal law already mentioned and published in God’s word: so also, sin having been retracted and abandoned through true repentance, and an active faith being posited by which the sinner flees to God’s clemency in Christ, that relation ceases through which the sinner was liable to the curse and divine wrath, and another arises through which he is pleasing to God and accepted unto eternal life—and that by force of another law, by which God also from eternity sanctioned that every sinner withdrawing from sin through true contrition, and earnestly imploring divine mercy, and embracing it through living and efficacious faith, should be immune from the penalties owed to sin, and should become pleasing and a friend to God, and should have a right to eternal life: which law God also took care to have published in his word.
pass_b_english: Remission = guilt-relation ends; a reconciling, life-accepting relation rises in its place.
Same relational logic under the eternal gospel law of contrition, mercy-seeking, and living faith.

choices.why: Gospel sanction vs law of penalty.
